This SHA-256 is the retry-domain digest of org, actor/client identifiers and an idempotency key. Authenticator return-object taint is propagated into public identity fields; no password verifier is derived or stored. Existing persisted idempotency identities must remain unchanged. Re-reviewed for PR #428 (Defty W1-b read authorization) against raw CodeQL run 42791251995 on commit 555f7c5b. The sink is textually identical and moves one line because agent-actions.ts imports spaceMembers; read_canvas now also requires room membership and an org-scoped canvas lookup. Mapping every location and flow step back through the branch diff reproduces the prior exact fingerprint, no flow step touches a changed line, and the hashed inputs remain org, actor/client identifiers and the idempotency key. Re-reviewed again for PR #428 against raw CodeQL run 42798401766 on commit 92e5af1f (after 1ff20dcf and 92e5af1f). The sink is textually identical and moves from line 341 to 342 because of the new resolveReadableRoom import. Mapping every location and flow step back through git diff 555f7c5b..92e5af1f reproduces the previously reviewed fingerprint; no flow step touches a changed line. agent-actions.ts gains one import (resolveReadableRoom), shifting flow steps one line, and the read_canvas block grows five lines, shifting later flow steps six lines; the canvas room resolver is not on the flow. The hashed inputs remain org, actor/client identifiers and the idempotency key.

These hashes index server-generated OAuth codes/access/refresh tokens created by randomToken using randomBytes(32), not low-entropy user passwords. Token lookup still checks authorization scope, expiry and revocation. SHA-256 for uniformly random 256-bit bearer tokens does not require a password KDF.

Only org ID, owner ID, provider and provider-subject identity are hashed into the retained principal digest. OAuth binding validation taints the whole record; actual access/refresh credentials are not hash inputs. The digest is an immutable account-identity fence, not password storage.

oauthDigest derives scoped account/storage identity and client-policy fingerprints. validateOAuthBinding contains only public binding metadata; oauthClientFingerprint explicitly omits client_secret. This is not a password verifier and cannot be changed without breaking retained account keys; caller inputs are pinned below.

The target is the exact Host-created opaque srcdoc iframe (allow-scripts without allow-same-origin), fixed canonical trusted script and escaped Host-origin metadata. Exact contentWindow/null-origin readiness plus current identity/authority gate one scoped MessagePort; stop revokes/removes only that frame. Global parent worker-src self/blob is explicit for SPA inheritance; child hash-only script CSP and connect-none confine the inherited Blob Worker. Author bytes never execute in the parent or document. Wildcard targets the opaque frame, not an arbitrary window; all supporting source is pinned. Persistent consent parsing changes only explicitly reviewed grant deadlines: null requires the literal until_revoked mode. Frame identity, opaque origin, finite Experience lease, one-port transfer and revocation gates remain unchanged. The 2026-10-17 renewal adds only a schema-validated target key for the read-only resource_refresh operation and a typed visibility-ended error; it neither changes frame creation, readiness, source, origin, port transfer or revocation nor permits target nomination for record writes. The 2026-10-20 re-review against run 39400742666 confirms this stop message carries only the existing session ID to the same Host-created opaque frame; teardown marks the lifetime stopped, revokes the bridge, closes the port and removes the frame. The source change only passes background_refresh_description into ExperienceConnectionSettings; it does not alter this sink or its frame confinement. The 2026-10-20 re-review for PR #389 (run 39467581550) confirms the sink only moved three lines: that change adds byte-formatting helpers above the component and rewords the private-access review copy and footer; it does not alter this sink, frame creation, readiness, origin, port transfer or revocation. Re-reviewed for Kit42 using raw CodeQL run 39562029913: all three sink fingerprints, locations and code flows are unchanged. The only mismatched supporting source is next.config.ts, where trusted build aliases move from mail helpers to Host-owned structured-address/safe-rich-text/safe-uri/safe-raster. CSP, worker-src, child confinement, origin/identity readiness, one-port transfer and revocation are unchanged. Explicit Host135 F1 re-review against raw CodeQL run 39665272733 confirms the three fingerprints, locations and code flows are unchanged. The changed component now reports bounded structured errors and retries ordinary app opening without a reconnect or permission endpoint. The changed startup helper pauses only the thirty-second visible rendering budget while hidden; it does not pause or extend finite session, exposure or consent deadlines. Visibility restoration still awaits suspension.live and current-authority checks before the unchanged locallyCurrent and one-start gates may transfer a port. Error notices remain Host text and cannot alter the target frame, Worker payload or scoped MessagePort. The exact Host-created allow-scripts-only opaque frame, trusted hash-constrained bootstrap, exact contentWindow/null-origin readiness, origin checks, lease identity and teardown revocation remain the security boundary. Re-reviewed for FX-A PR #410 against fresh raw CodeQL run 39689516157 on commit f4c17114708faeef49600158c0a269df45aa1786. The three existing frame sinks move exactly three lines; normalizing those location and flow line offsets reproduces each prior exact fingerprint. Query, message, columns, partial fingerprints and every inner flow step are unchanged. Current-screen access state and feature-local read-error reporting do not change the Host-created allow-scripts-only opaque iframe, exact contentWindow/null-origin readiness, current identity/lease/visibility checks, one-port transfer or teardown revocation. No grant or finite authority deadline is extended. Re-reviewed for the Email-ready release PR #424 against raw CodeQL run 41879227567. The three frame sinks are textually identical and move exactly 43 lines because the component now dispatches validated Kit connection_action buttons (Reconnect navigates the top-level page to the Host begin URL returned by the existing exact-origin connection flow; restore_access opens the Host Restore access review dialog) and passes per-account health into settings. The bridge only accepts the schema-validated connection_action field, and the bootstrap script raises the worker_source size bound from 98304 to 114688 bytes to match the 112 KiB Kit cap. Frame creation, the allow-scripts-only opaque srcdoc, exact contentWindow/null-origin readiness, identity/lease/visibility checks, one-port transfer and teardown revocation are unchanged, and no grant or finite authority deadline is extended. Re-reviewed for PR #424 against raw CodeQL run 42174633201 on commit 00afb2306a. The three frame sinks are textually identical and move exactly 14 lines. The component now delegates connection-action handling to the Host app-experience-connection-action library, parses catalog targets before use, and adds Host-side background-access recovery. None of that touches the opaque srcdoc frame, exact contentWindow/null-origin readiness, identity/lease/visibility checks, one-port transfer or teardown revocation, and no other pinned source for these findings changed.

This regex is an assertion over a fixed returned OAuth fixture URL, not the authorization-origin allowlist. Production connection begin parses URL and requires exact reviewed origin and callback state; the current production flow source is pinned below. Persistent durable scope parsing does not loosen OAuth navigation: Begin and callback deadlines remain finite, and exact parsed authorization origin plus a single exact callback-state parameter are still required. Re-reviewed for PR #424 against raw CodeQL run 41879227567: the fingerprint and location are unchanged. app-connection-session-flow.ts adds beginAppConnection, a thin wrapper that loads the flow and returns flow.begin(targetKey); begin still parses the URL and requires the exact reviewed authorization origin and a single exact callback-state parameter. The test regex remains an assertion over a fixed fixture URL.
